thread:
Samir Patel: Quick sync — we need to pick a consistent exposure strategy for internal APIs that power the Console. REST gateway vs direct gRPC surface? Pros/cons and rollout UX implications.

Maria Chen: Short take: gRPC internally + small REST facade at edge. Less duplication, clearer contracts. but client teams hate non-HTTP3-friendly tooling. :shrug: 

Devin Park: +1 to contract clarity. But think about telemetry and quotas — Envoy transcoding kills trace continuity and adds overhead. If we do REST->gRPC, we must preserve trace IDs and token attribution.

Elaine Ortiz: This matters for rollouts too. If we expose gRPC directly to Console, canarying model/version per-route becomes easier (we can route by proto package + method). With a REST facade we need mapping layer and extra feature flags.

Benji (eng-platform): Ops perspective: latency budget. Transcoding adds ~6-12ms p99 on our tests with current proxies. For most Console flows that's noticeable. But avoid huge SDK churn for product teams.

Samir Patel: Good call on traces and quotas. Devs want simple fetch() examples. But platform wants strong typing and schema evolution safety (protobufs).

Devin Park: What if we standardize on protobuf-first and generate a tiny HTTP shim that keeps endpoints human-friendly, e.g. /v1/users:list -> POST /v1/users:list with proto body, and keep path conventions for autogen? That buys SDK ergonomics, keeps proto safety, and reduces complex transcoding rules.

Maria Chen: I like the tiny shim idea but we need clear migration docs. Also console UX for rollouts — teams should be able to flip a canary by model version or by route percentage from the Console, not just config files. That requires the control plane to understand mapping from REST route -> proto method.

Elaine Ortiz: Telemetry implications: instrument at the cluster ingress and at the runtime. We'll attach both request-level attributes: route, proto_method, model_variant, customer_tier. Then Console dashboards can slice by model_variant during a rollout.

Benji (eng-platform): Quotas: we should propagate token/tenant info as a native header from edge to runtime so quota enforcement can be centralized. Suggest header X-Tenant-Id, X-Quota-Key and preserve via trusted hop. Also gate mismatch cases with a 422 and a clear error body for clients.

Samir Patel: Can we get a spike to measure end-to-end: (a) gRPC-only internal surface, (b) REST facade shim (autogen), (c) full Envoy transcoding. Measure p50/p95/p99 + trace propagation and cost delta. Who can own?

Devin Park: I can run the spike this week. Plan: generate a small service with 6 methods (sync/stream combos), implement the three exposure modes, run load with realistic token sizes and KV cache patterns. Will add tracing headers: x-request-id + x-tenant-id and show end-to-end spans.

Maria Chen: Please also capture rollout UX friction: how many clicks to enable canary by method vs by route mapping. I'll mock the Console flow and list necessary control plane APIs.

Elaine Ortiz: I'll write the telemetry schema we need and list dashboard panels: latency by method/model_variant, error budget burn, quota consumption per-tenant, request attribution. Put it in a short RFC once spike data in.

Benji (eng-platform): ops will simulate quota anomalies and failure cases (broken mapping, missing header) and we will validate graceful degradation and clear logs.

deploy-bot: CI check started for spike branch: spike/ig/exposure-strategies (build + basic e2e).

Samir Patel: Excellent. Action items: Devin spike (owner), Maria console UX mock, Elaine telemetry schema, Benji ops tests. We'll reconvene next Tue. Thanks all. :rocket:
